cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: Stewarding both — tending what you carry through form, keeping two goods in careful balance rather than force.
cells.place: Where you know which star you're steering by, and what you tend is orientation, not fantasy.
cells.ask: Name one person whose sacrifice has been making your work possible, and let them hear it honored — release then flows from completion, surrender as fulfillment rather than a loss, because tending has been witnessed.
cells.core: You're the one tending what grows here — keeping two demands held in balance through care, not force. Not controlling the outcome, and not letting it run unattended. The work arrives in form because you brought it there, which is why it lasts.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing here, and you tend it by hand, not by force.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: Tending ahead of the season — managing what hasn't come up yet, gripping the form before it's formed.
cells.place: Standing where the pull toward light is real, but you've turned it into a deadline instead of a direction.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're tending finish on its own timing before you touch it again — vision flows from genuine integration, dreaming because what you've loved has been fully felt, not because you're already bracing for the next season.
cells.core: You're tending things that haven't come up yet. Every demand gets handled before it arrives, every form held tight enough to survive a future you're already living in — and the care is costing you the thing care was for. The tending has replaced the growing.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding what hasn't grown yet, and it can't breathe.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: Tending something you stopped shaping — stewardship left running in a room you no longer enter.
cells.place: Where the pull toward light used to point, and now you only remember the direction without following it.
cells.ask: Keep hoping for one thing, even without evidence — persistence through aspiration is strength, and radiance flows from genuine development, shining because what you've cultivated actually reached its end.
cells.core: You know something is worth tending, and you've stopped tending it. Somewhere behind you is a season where the work didn't return, and you're still taking instruction from that season. The pull toward light hasn't gone anywhere; the following did.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending a thing you still know is worth it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: Stewarding without claiming it — tending the form so quietly that the care looks like it happens by itself.
cells.place: Already oriented toward the light you'd say you're still looking for, already steering by a star you haven't named.
cells.ask: Own one thing you've been tending as done by you, and let it be seen — release flows naturally from completion, surrender as fulfillment, and completion can only be honored if the one who did the work will name it.
cells.core: You're already tending what grows around you — deciding what holds, what's carried forward, what gets protection — and you describe it as if it were just upkeep. The stewardship is running; the claim on it isn't. The one person not crediting the care is the one giving it.
cells.sheetLine: The tending is yours. You're calling it just how things run.
